_readme: Independent ground truth for the 3 random-forest/rule disagreements, hand-checked against raw element counts (grep note/measure/identifier/classification/perfMedium) rather than re-running detectEncodingStyle. Used by ml_style.py --hand-labels to report accuracy against labels the classifier was never trained or folded against, closing the circularity gap noted in the draft report (5.8).

mei50_Telemann_Concert.mei.label: notation
mei50_Telemann_Concert.mei.evidence: 6320 <note> elements across 230 measures vs only 5 metadata elements (identifier/classification/perfMedium). Overwhelmingly a notated score with a thin bibliographic wrapper; a human cataloguer would call this notation-style, not catalogue-style.

mei51_Schubert_Erlkoenig.mei.label: notation
mei51_Schubert_Erlkoenig.mei.evidence: 138 <note> elements across 30 measures vs 3 metadata elements. Same pattern as Telemann: a full song setting with minimal header, not a catalogue entry.

SE_26_Debussy_GolliwoggsCakewalk.mei.label: notation
SE_26_Debussy_GolliwoggsCakewalk.mei.evidence: 1374 <note> elements across 129 measures vs 9 metadata elements including a populated workDesc/work block. Genuinely hybrid in structure (both rich notation and a real work record), but by volume this is a notated score, not a bibliographic record.

freidi_core_mov9.xml.label: notation
freidi_core_mov9.xml.evidence: 6284 <note> elements across 199 measures, no workList and only scattered work-adjacent text; one movement of a full opera encoding, overwhelmingly notation by volume despite the rule folding it to catalogue.
